Samantha —

Thanks for the CSV, this is exactly the kind of traffic sample we need. I'm attaching a short graded scaling proposal and a model workbook with our assumptions. High-level takeaways up-front:

- Fingerprint shape: mixed tail with ~5% of requests generating 60% of token volume (typical for embedding-batched workloads).
- Recommended grades:
  * Grade A (steady): sustain 120k tokens/s, ~8x T4-equivalent GPUs (quantized), target p95 gen latency 220ms.
  * Grade B (elevated): sustain 360k tokens/s with burst headroom, ~24x GPUs with warm-pool 4 nodes ready (warmup amortized).
  * Grade C (surge/protect): absorb 800k tokens/s short-window spikes via admission control + prewarmed spare nodes (fallback to cheaper quantized variant).
- Warm-pool policy: maintain rolling warmers sized to 20% of expected burst concurrency; use fast ramp (preemptive start) based on traffic derivative detection.
- Network: reserve an egress headroom of 6Gbps per 100k tokens/s of peak to cover artifacts + cache misses; cross-connect should allow burst ceilings ~2x baseline.

Attachments: graded_scaling_model.xlsx, vpc-network-diagram.png (I've added inline assumptions). Can Marissa and Jonas weigh-in on the network and admission-control knobs? Karthik: any gotchas on warm-pool costs or caching that would materially change node counts?

If this looks good, propose a 30m alignment Wednesday 11 AM PT to sync with your infra team.

Cheers,
Alex
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alex / Samantha —

Quick network checklist from ops perspective:
- Cross-connect sizing: aim for 10Gbps headroom if you expect sustained Grade B traffic; 1G/100k tokens/s underestimates due to checkpoint and artifact transfers.
- Egress policing: set burst token bucket with token refill tied to observed QPS derivative; enforce per-tenant egress caps to avoid noisy-neighbor egress storms.
- MTU and NIC offload: enable jumbo frames on the private subnet for embedding payloads > MTU to reduce CPU pressure.

Jonas: recommend we add a soft-admission layer at the ingress (reject or queue requests above Grade B sustained) and a fail-open policy to Grade C fallback model in service catalog. Also add a cache warmup job as soon as we detect a ramp (sampled traffic warm-up).

Samantha — I'll bring an exploded egress table to the Wed call.

—Marissa
Senior Infra Ops, Redwood Inference

Marissa / team —

Couple of operational edge notes:
- Warm-pool amortization: we assume 45–60s warmup for quantized variants on our runtime; if your job patterns are sub-30s spikes we should lean into admission + queued responses rather than prewarming a large fleet.
- Storage egress: what % of requests hit cold cache matters a lot; I modeled 15% cold cache for the spreadsheet. If ScaleEdge runs nightly bulk updates, that bumps network by ~25%.
- Cost tradeoff: for Grade C protection we recommend 40% cheaper spot-like GPU reservations (non-preemptible within your VPC) to keep tail SLOs without full on-demand costs.

I'll update the workbook with two sensitivity knobs and a short Monte Carlo for burst frequency before the call.

-Jonas
Head of Platform Reliability
